degenerate_armour_plate.flavour: A slab of neutronium that should, by rights, explode back into a cloud of free neutrons the moment it leaves a star. The spacetime-alloy frame keeps the pressure on, so the plate stays degenerate: neutrons packed shoulder to shoulder, refusing by the Pauli principle to be squeezed any further. It weighs far more than its size suggests and rings like nothing at all when struck.
degenerate_armour_plate.discovery: Neutronium decompresses violently outside a star, so I tried caging a block in spacetime alloy and letting the Casimir Vacuum Press hold the vacuum around it. The neutrons stayed locked. Anything that can survive a compact star's interior can survive me.

pentaquark_shard.flavour: Four quarks and an antiquark, bound into one hadron that real accelerators only glimpse as a bump in a decay spectrum. Here the bump has been frozen into a glittering shard. It hums faintly against the palm, as if the five constituents are still arguing over who holds whom, and the colour charge never quite settles.
pentaquark_shard.discovery: Smashing strange matter into antimatter inside the Hyperion Synchrotron, I saw a resonance in the debris that matched no ordinary baryon. Pouring quark-gluon plasma over the collision point, then cooling it with entangled photons, let the five-quark state crystallise before it fell apart.

glueball_core.flavour: Gluons carry the very colour charge they mediate, so in principle they can bind to one another with no quarks at all. This is that bound state: a knot of pure strong force, heavy and warm, with nothing inside it but the glue. Lattice QCD predicted it for decades; I am holding one.
glueball_core.discovery: I stripped the quarks out of a quark-gluon plasma beam using strange matter as a sink and a qubit to tag what remained. Most runs left nothing. One left a dense, colourless sphere of self-interacting gluons that refused to decay.

hyperon_crystal.flavour: Baryons in which at least one ordinary quark has been swapped for a strange one: lambdas, sigmas, xis, packed into a lattice. Strangeness adds mass and a slow, stubborn weak decay that these crystals simply postpone. The faces are cold, the inside feels heavier than the outside, and it is never quite still.
hyperon_crystal.discovery: Feeding strange matter and a sterile neutrino through the synchrotron, I tried to coax strange quarks into ordinary baryons. Tachyon crystal stretched the decay clock long enough for the hyperons to settle into a lattice instead of decaying.

hypernova_alloy_ingot.flavour: Cosmic neutronium, spacetime alloy, glueballs, hyperons and a superheavy metal, all melted together above the temperature at which matter can still be said to have a melting point. The ingot never cools. Its glow is the afterimage of a collapsing star that the metal seems to remember, and it is warm through any glove.
hypernova_alloy_ingot.discovery: The Transcendent Plasma Forge finally ran hot enough that the ingredients stopped behaving as separate materials. I dropped in a supernova remnant to seed the melt and an alloy of everything I had came out, still shining long after the forge shut down.

transcendent_metal_ingot.flavour: In the forge, above stellar-core temperatures, properties like hardness and conductivity stop being fixed and start being chosen. This ingot is what a metal looks like when someone else chose them. It weighs exactly what the forge decided, and feels faintly as though it might change its mind.
transcendent_metal_ingot.discovery: I fed the forge a hypernova alloy and things that are barely matter at all: an aleph-null shard, Russell's paradox, a cosmic processor. The processor set the rules, the paradox loosened the old ones, and the metal accepted whatever properties it was given.

horizon_shard.flavour: A sliver of event horizon, carried out of a black hole simulating a universe of its own. By the holographic principle the horizon area stores everything that ever fell inward, so this shard is less a surface than an archive. It is black from every angle and slightly cold, as Hawking radiation would predict.
horizon_shard.discovery: The Eye of the Event Horizon computes a whole universe on a black hole's surface. Seeding a fresh simulation with a universe seed, liquid spacetime and an existing shard, I found a new sliver of horizon peeled off as the simulated cosmos ended.

natural_number_lattice.flavour: Zero, then the successor of zero, then the successor of that, and on forever. Peano needed nothing more to build all of arithmetic, and this lattice is that chain made solid: a crystal that keeps growing a new node at the end however far along you look. It feels orderly in a way no rock ever does.
natural_number_lattice.discovery: I first found these lattices lying in the vaults of the Platonic Realm, where numbers simply exist. Back home, the Peano Arithmetic Engine taught me to grow them from an axiom stone and a qubit: one rule for zero, one for the next.

integer_ring.flavour: Every natural number paired with its mirror image below zero, closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication. The ring has a satisfying symmetry: turn it over and every number becomes its negative. Being a ring, you can add or multiply any two elements and never fall out of it.
integer_ring.discovery: Subtraction kept breaking the natural numbers; three minus five had nowhere to go. Feeding an antimatter pellet into the engine alongside a natural lattice gave each number an opposite, the way antimatter gives each particle one.

rational_field.flavour: Every fraction of one integer by another, which is enough to divide by anything except zero. Between any two rationals there is another, so the field is dense everywhere, yet the square root of two is nowhere in it. It shimmers like a fine mesh that hides countless holes.
rational_field.discovery: I needed division, so I let a Casimir plate split the integer ring into finer and finer slices, mimicking how the vacuum between plates is divided into modes. Every ratio appeared, and with them, the unsettling gaps between them.

real_continuum.flavour: The rationals with every gap filled: every limit of every convergent sequence now lands somewhere. That includes the transcendentals, which no polynomial can reach and which had to be brought in from the Platonic Realm. Running a finger along it, there is no texture at all, because there is nowhere for a gap to be.
real_continuum.discovery: Following Dedekind, I cut the rational field at every possible point and asked the Analytic Continuator to fill each cut. Golden-ratio glass supplied the irrationals and a Bose-Einstein condensate let the whole line settle into a single smooth state.

imaginary_unit.flavour: A number whose square is minus one, which sounds like nonsense until you notice that it simply rotates the number line by a right angle. A tachyon's mass is imaginary, and this tiny bead was distilled from exactly that. It looks perfectly ordinary until you turn it, when it seems to point somewhere sideways.
imaginary_unit.discovery: A tachyon's rest mass squared is negative, so its mass itself must be an imaginary number. I condensed tachyon flux over a tachyon crystal and pinned the result against the real continuum, and the leftover factor was i.

complex_plane.flavour: The real line, with the imaginary unit laid at right angles across it, forming a flat sheet of numbers. On this plane every polynomial has all its roots, multiplication is rotation and scaling, and smooth functions become astonishingly rigid. It feels like a perfectly flat, perfectly thin pane of glass.
complex_plane.discovery: With i in hand, the obvious step was to cross it with the real continuum. The Analytic Continuator held the two at right angles in a condensate until they fused into one field of numbers, two dimensions wide.

quaternion_crystal.flavour: Hamilton's numbers: one real part and three imaginary units i, j and k, which multiply in a fixed cycle and do not commute. Swap the order and the sign flips. Rotations in three dimensions are just quaternion multiplication, so the crystal turns in the hand with an uncanny smoothness and never gimbal-locks.
quaternion_crystal.discovery: Trying to extend the complex plane into three dimensions failed, as it did for Hamilton, until I added a fourth. A magnetic monopole supplied the twist that lets ij differ from ji, and the condensate held it steady.

octonion_crystal.flavour: Eight-dimensional numbers, built by doubling quaternions once more. Multiplication stops even associating, so the order you group products in matters. Yet every non-zero octonion still has an inverse; they are the last and largest normed division algebra. The crystal is beautiful and slightly unsettling to look at for long.
octonion_crystal.discovery: Doubling the quaternions by the Cayley-Dickson trick needed room for eight dimensions, which a Calabi-Yau manifold and some exotic matter provided. A prime shard stabilised the multiplication table. Hurwitz says there is nothing beyond this that still divides.

surreal_number.flavour: Conway built every number from two sets, a left and a right, and found that the reals, the infinite ordinals and the infinitesimals all fit into one ordered field. This gem contains all of them. It is impossibly dense, endlessly fine, and every attempt to find its edge reveals another number there.
surreal_number.discovery: The Cantor Diagonalizer was the only machine with room for this. I fed it octonions, the reals, an aleph-null shard and an infinitesimal, and let dark energy keep expanding the space between them until every gap was a number.

prime_shard.flavour: A sliver of a number divisible only by one and itself. Primes are the atoms of arithmetic: every whole number factors into them in exactly one way. In the Platonic Realm they grow wild in irregular clusters; out here they must be sieved. Each shard is sharp-edged and refuses to split.
prime_shard.discovery: I first found these crystals scattered in the Platonic Realm's vaults and in the debris of Axiom Sentinels. Later I learned to sieve them out of a natural number lattice with a quantum processor, Eratosthenes style, discarding every multiple.

modular_form.flavour: A function on the complex upper half-plane with so much symmetry that it is almost forced to be what it is. Modular forms connect primes, elliptic curves and string partition functions, and Wiles used them to prove Fermat's Last Theorem. This one is a slowly turning tiling of curved triangles.
modular_form.discovery: Combining a Fourier series with primes on the complex plane, I hoped for a function whose coefficients counted something arithmetic. The Analytic Continuator returned one invariant under the whole modular group, with prime patterns hiding in its expansion.

riemann_zeta_crystal.flavour: The zeta function encodes the distribution of primes in its zeros. Riemann conjectured that every non-trivial zero has real part exactly one half; nobody has proved it. This crystal grew in a single perfectly straight line, and every zero I have checked sits on it. It is cold and perfectly balanced.
riemann_zeta_crystal.discovery: Analytically continuing the sum over primes past where it converges took a modular form, the complex plane and superfluid helium to damp the noise. The crystal that formed grew along the critical line. I keep looking for a zero off it.

transcendental_crystal.flavour: Pi, e and their relatives: numbers no polynomial with integer coefficients will ever produce. Almost every real number is transcendental, yet proving any particular one is hard. The crystal never repeats its pattern, however closely you look, and it seems to go on past its own surface.
transcendental_crystal.discovery: I only ever found these in the Platonic Realm, tucked in Euclid's vaults and Hilbert's archives. No machine of mine can build one from algebra alone, which is exactly what transcendental means.

infinitesimal.flavour: Smaller than every positive real, and yet not zero. Leibniz used them freely; Weierstrass banished them; Robinson brought them back rigorously as non-standard analysis. The grain looks like nothing at all, and the closer you look the further away it seems to be.
infinitesimal.discovery: I wanted the step size in a derivative to be truly smaller than anything. The Analytic Continuator pressed the real continuum against a quantum dot under superfluid helium, and squeezed out a number below every real but still above zero.

function_graph.flavour: A rule that sends each input to exactly one output, drawn as a curve of light through the plane. Some are smooth, some are jagged, and some are discontinuous everywhere. It hangs in the air as a luminous thread that never doubles back on itself vertically.
function_graph.discovery: A photonic neuron fires once for each input it is given; aimed across the real continuum, it traced every input to its output. The Analytic Continuator kept the beam as a permanent curve rather than a flash.

derivative_operator.flavour: Take a function, look at it on a smaller and smaller scale until it looks straight, and record the slope. That is the derivative, and this operator does it at every point at once. It feels like a lens: everything seen through it is reduced to how fast it is changing.
derivative_operator.discovery: Dividing a function graph's rise by its run over an infinitesimal step gave exactly the instantaneous slope I wanted. Newton and Leibniz argued over credit; the Analytic Continuator just does it.

integral_operator.flavour: The opposite of a derivative: chop a curve into infinitely many infinitesimal strips and sum their areas. The fundamental theorem of calculus says these two operators undo each other. This one is smooth and heavy, like a closed scroll of everything a function has ever accumulated.
integral_operator.discovery: Stacking infinitesimal slices under a function graph, I found the total area converged to a single number however fine I cut. The Analytic Continuator made the sum permanent, and running it backwards gave me the derivative again.

fourier_series.flavour: Fourier claimed any periodic signal could be written as a sum of sines and cosines, and he was almost right. This series holds infinitely many harmonics in balance, each one a quiet tone. Hold it to your ear and it hums every frequency at once, so quietly that it sounds like silence.
fourier_series.discovery: Integrating a function graph against waves on the complex plane gave me one coefficient for each frequency. Adding the waves back together rebuilt the original curve exactly, and the Continuator stored the whole spectrum.

fractal_set.flavour: Iterate z goes to z squared plus c, and colour each point by whether it escapes. The boundary that results is infinitely detailed: zoom in anywhere and new spirals, filaments and tiny copies of the whole appear. Holding it, the edges seem fuzzy, and they never sharpen however closely you look.
fractal_set.discovery: Running a Koch crystal's self-similar rule through a function graph on the complex plane, I asked the Analytic Continuator which points stayed bounded. The answer was the Mandelbrot set, coastlines within coastlines.

fractal_dust.flavour: Grit with the same structure at every scale: each grain is made of smaller grains arranged exactly like the whole pile. Its dimension is not a whole number, somewhere between a scattering of points and a line. It sifts strangely, never quite settling, as if there is always more of it.
fractal_dust.discovery: The first handful came from a Fractal Wyrm I had cut down in the Platonic Realm, and from shelves in the old vaults. Later I learned to shave it from fractal lattice blocks with the Planck-Scale Cutter, helium keeping the cuts clean.

differential_manifold.flavour: A space that looks flat if you look closely enough, though it may curve in any way overall. Calculus works on each small flat patch, and the patches stitch together smoothly. Einstein wrote relativity on exactly this kind of stage. The object folds and flexes in the hand without ever creasing.
differential_manifold.discovery: I wanted calculus on a curved surface, so I glued derivative and integral operators onto a topological insulator patch by patch. The condensate smoothed the seams until no point could tell it was anywhere special.

mobius_strip.flavour: Take a strip, give it a half-twist and join the ends: it now has only one side and one edge. Trace the middle with a finger and you return to where you started, but on what was the other face. Cut it down the centre and it stays in one piece.
mobius_strip.discovery: The Metamaterial Weaver let me twist a sheet so its surface conducted like a topological insulator along a single path. A function graph guided the half-twist; when the ends met, both faces had become one.

klein_bottle.flavour: A bottle whose neck passes through its own side to join the base from inside, so that inside and outside are the same surface. In three dimensions it must cross itself; in four it does not. This one was built in four, so its glass never touches itself and nothing can be poured into it.
klein_bottle.discovery: Gluing two Mobius strips edge to edge needed a fourth dimension to avoid self-intersection. The Tesseract Assembler supplied it, with exotic matter to hold the surface open while I joined them.

axiom_schema.flavour: The starting assumptions of a system, written out as patterns that stand for infinitely many individual axioms. Change one and you change what can be proved. The slate is plain and heavy, and every line carved on it is accepted without proof.
axiom_schema.discovery: I found my first schemas in Euclid's vault and among the debris of Axiom Sentinels. Building my own meant encoding natural number rules into a qubit until the Formal Proof Assistant would accept them as given.

empty_set.flavour: The set with nothing in it. From it alone, by taking sets of sets, you can build every number and every structure in mathematics. It is surprisingly heavy for something containing nothing, and the eye slides off it.
empty_set.discovery: A Void Wraith leaves behind a kind of absence. Feeding that essence to the Formal Proof Assistant, I asked it to collect every element present. It returned a set and confirmed that it was empty.

power_set.flavour: The set of all subsets of a set. Cantor proved it is always strictly larger than the set itself, even when the original is infinite. Turn it over and it seems to contain more than could possibly fit in it.
power_set.discovery: I asked the Formal Proof Assistant to list every subset of a natural number lattice, starting with the empty set. A proof tree confirmed what Cantor showed: no list of them could ever be complete.

formal_proof_tree.flavour: A proof written so carefully that every step cites the rule that justifies it, branching back to axioms at the leaves. Machines check these line by line; mathematicians tend to trust them and move on. The tree is cool and heavy and it never contradicts itself.
formal_proof_tree.discovery: Mathematicians skip steps; I wanted a proof with none. Feeding an axiom schema and a function graph into a quantum processor, and wetting it with synaptic fluid, gave me a tree where every leaf was an axiom.

continuum_shard.flavour: A shard whose size is that of the real line, two to the power aleph-null. Cantor guessed nothing lay between it and the countable infinity; Godel and Cohen proved the usual axioms cannot decide. The shard looks different every time you examine it, as if politely refusing to commit.
continuum_shard.discovery: Taking the power set of an aleph-null shard should give the reals; it did, but the Cantor Diagonalizer refused to say whether omega-one fit between them. Dark energy kept it from collapsing while I waited. I also found pieces in the Ordinal Spire.

axiom_of_choice.flavour: Given any collection of non-empty sets, you may choose one element from each, even when no rule tells you which. It seems harmless, yet it implies that a sphere can be cut into finitely many pieces and reassembled into two spheres. The token feels decisive.
axiom_of_choice.discovery: I asked the Formal Proof Assistant to choose a point from each piece of the continuum and it could not without an extra axiom. I wrote one in and it immediately proved Banach-Tarski.

category_lattice.flavour: Objects connected by arrows, with the only rule being that arrows compose. Numbers, spaces, groups and programs all form categories, and theorems about one often transfer to the others. The lattice looks almost bare: dots and arrows, and nothing else.
category_lattice.discovery: I noticed that function graphs, power sets and axiom schemas all had the same shape: things and maps between them. The Formal Proof Assistant abstracted that shape into a lattice of objects and arrows.

functor_bridge.flavour: A map between categories that sends objects to objects and arrows to arrows while respecting composition. It lets you translate a hard problem in one area of mathematics into an easier one elsewhere. The bridge is narrow, sturdy and arched in a way that suggests symmetry.
functor_bridge.discovery: I needed a structured way to pass from a category to a manifold to the octonions. The Formal Proof Assistant found a functor that carried every arrow over without breaking a composition.

topos.flavour: A category so rich it behaves like its own universe of sets, with its own internal logic. In some toposes the law of the excluded middle fails; in others, every function is continuous. Holding one, ordinary truths feel negotiable.
topos.discovery: Wrapping a functor bridge around a Klein bottle and the continuum, I found a structure where a Godel sentence could be decided. The Formal Proof Assistant called it a topos: a universe with its own rules of truth.

up_down_quarks.flavour: The two lightest quark flavours, carrying charges of plus two-thirds and minus one-third. Two ups and a down make a proton; two downs and an up make a neutron; so nearly every atom ever touched is built from these. Confinement means they never appear alone, and the pair sits in the palm with a stubborn, sticky pull.
up_down_quarks.discovery: Virtual quarks from the Quantum Foam vanish almost as soon as they appear. Running them through the Particle Spectrometer under superfluid helium, I could sort them by mass, and the two lightest flavours came out first and most often.

strange_charm_quarks.flavour: The second generation: copies of the up and down with more mass and new quantum numbers, strangeness and charm. Outside strange matter they decay in a fraction of an instant through the weak force. These are held together, faintly fizzing, as if impatient to become something lighter.
strange_charm_quarks.discovery: Sorting virtual quarks by mass, I noticed a heavier pair in the Spectrometer's readout. The charm quark took experimentalists by surprise in 1974; it took me by surprise too, until the helium cooled them enough to keep.

bottom_top_quarks.flavour: The third and final generation. The bottom is heavy; the top is as massive as a gold atom and decays before it can form a hadron. They are rarer than anything else in the Standard Model, and holding them feels like holding a pair of collapsing weights.
bottom_top_quarks.discovery: The second generation was not enough; colliding strange and charm quarks with pentaquarks in the Hyperion Synchrotron pushed collision energy high enough. Quark-gluon plasma caught the heaviest quarks before they could decay.

lepton_triplet.flavour: Electron, muon and tau, three charged leptons differing only in mass, each paired with its own neutrino. None of them feel the strong force. The triplet hangs together loosely, and the neutrinos seem to drift straight through my hand without noticing.
lepton_triplet.discovery: Neutrino flux passes through almost everything, so I used a sterile neutrino as a bait and antimatter to tag charged partners. The Particle Spectrometer separated three charged leptons, each shadowed by its neutrino flavour.

gauge_boson_cluster.flavour: Photon, gluon, W and Z: the particles that carry electromagnetism and the strong and weak forces. Each is the ripple of a symmetry in its field. The cluster is lively and restless in the hand, pushing and pulling in ways that do not quite add up to any single force.
gauge_boson_cluster.discovery: Entangled photons gave me the photon; a glueball core gave me gluons; quark-gluon plasma at high energy supplied the W and Z. The Particle Spectrometer collected all four force carriers into a single cluster.

higgs_boson_crystal.flavour: An excitation of the Higgs field, which fills all of space and gives particles their mass by dragging on them. Normally it decays in less than a zeptosecond. This crystal caught one before it could, and it is heavy in a way that seems to come from the field around it rather than the crystal.
higgs_boson_crystal.discovery: The Higgs couples most strongly to the heaviest particles, so I fed top quarks, gauge bosons and a Higgs field capacitor into the Hyperion Synchrotron. In the debris, a resonance I had been looking for froze solid.

standard_model_matrix.flavour: Six quarks, six leptons, the gauge bosons and the Higgs, arranged in one ordered lattice. It explains nearly every experiment ever done, and yet leaves out gravity, dark matter, and why there are three generations at all. The matrix is tidy, elegant and unsatisfying.
standard_model_matrix.discovery: With every particle in hand, I fed them into the Femtoscale Assembly Line to see if they would fit together. They did, in a pattern of three generations and a few forces, and the gaps were exactly where gravity and dark matter should be.

superpartner_shard.flavour: Supersymmetry pairs every boson with a fermion and every fermion with a boson. The lightest such partner, the neutralino, would be stable, invisible and heavy: an ideal candidate for dark matter. The shard is almost weightless in light but seems far heavier when you try to move it.
superpartner_shard.discovery: Colliding the Standard Model matrix with dark matter through a dark matter lens, I searched for something that interacted only weakly. A heavy neutral partner appeared, and it matched dark matter perfectly.

grand_unified_core.flavour: At sufficiently high energy, the electromagnetic, weak and strong couplings run together and meet. Grand unified theories predict magnetic monopoles and proton decay as a consequence. The core is bright and calm, three forces resting in a single symmetry.
grand_unified_core.discovery: Running the Standard Model's couplings upward with superpartners included, I saw them converge. In the Tesseract Assembler, a monopole and a quantum string held the high-energy state long enough to crystallise it.

lorentz_transform_crystal.flavour: The rules for how space and time look to someone moving at a different speed: lengths contract, clocks slow and simultaneity stops being universal. This crystal is moving near light speed in some frame, and in mine it appears squashed, its internal clocks ticking visibly slowly.
lorentz_transform_crystal.discovery: Entangled photons gave me a clock that always moved at light speed; tachyon flux gave me one that moved faster. The Tensor Calculus Engine found the transformation that kept the speed of light the same for both.

minkowski_lattice.flavour: Space and time woven into a single four-dimensional geometry, with a light cone at every point separating the reachable future from the forbidden elsewhere. The lattice is flat but strange: distances can be zero between distinct events, and time behaves like an imaginary direction.
minkowski_lattice.discovery: Minkowski realised Lorentz transformations were just rotations in a four-dimensional spacetime. I combined Lorentz crystals with a differential manifold and quaternions in the Tensor Calculus Engine, and the light cones appeared.

metric_tensor.flavour: The object that tells you how to measure distance and time in curved spacetime: feed it two directions and it returns a number. In flat space it is simple; around stars and black holes it varies from point to point. The tensor is smooth and slightly warped when held.
metric_tensor.discovery: Flat Minkowski geometry was not enough near massive things. I differentiated the lattice and weighted it with a neutronium plate, and the Tensor Calculus Engine returned the curved metric that described it.

riemann_curvature_tensor.flavour: Carry an arrow around a small loop on a curved surface and it comes back rotated. The Riemann tensor measures exactly how much, at every point and in every direction. It is the precise mathematical meaning of curvature, and handling it feels like handling the shape of a surface directly.
riemann_curvature_tensor.discovery: Differentiating the metric twice and letting it orbit a micro singularity, I tracked how parallel-transported vectors rotated. The Tensor Calculus Engine summarised the effect in a single, many-indexed tensor.

einstein_field_core.flavour: Einstein's field equations relate the curvature of spacetime to the energy and momentum it contains. Matter tells spacetime how to curve; spacetime tells matter how to move. The core holds both sides, and anything near it seems to tilt slightly toward it.
einstein_field_core.discovery: I integrated the Riemann tensor over a stellar core and set curvature equal to energy density. Exotic matter kept the solution from collapsing, and the Tensor Calculus Engine produced the full field equations.

gravitational_wave_crystal.flavour: A ripple in spacetime itself, stretching and squeezing distances as it passes, frozen mid-oscillation. LIGO detected the first in 2015 from two merging black holes. The crystal pulses gently, alternately longer and shorter, as if breathing.
gravitational_wave_crystal.discovery: Two spinning micro singularities in the Kugelblitz Chamber spiralled together and merged. Hawking radiation lit the scene, and the field equations captured the outgoing ripple before it escaped.

kerr_metric_shard.flavour: The exact solution for spacetime around a rotating black hole, found by Roy Kerr in 1963. Near it, spacetime itself is dragged around, and inside the ergosphere nothing can stand still. The shard spins slightly in the hand, even when perfectly balanced.
kerr_metric_shard.discovery: Feeding a Penrose spindle and a micro singularity through the Tensor Calculus Engine with the field equations, I asked for a solution with spin. The answer, an ergosphere and frame dragging, was the Kerr metric.

protostar_core.flavour: A collapsing knot of nebular gas, compressing under its own gravity and heating as it falls inward. It glows deep red, hot enough to shine but not yet hot enough for hydrogen fusion. The core feels warm and dense and is slowly, steadily shrinking.
protostar_core.discovery: I seeded nebular gas with degenerate matter and a graviton crystal in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber, hoping it would collapse. It did, warming as it contracted, and stopped just short of ignition.

red_giant_envelope.flavour: When a star exhausts the hydrogen in its core it swells, and its outer layers expand and cool to a dull red. The Sun will do this in about five billion years. The envelope is enormous and tenuous, a thin, glowing fog that barely seems to weigh anything.
red_giant_envelope.discovery: Running a stellar core in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber past hydrogen exhaustion, I watched its outer layers puff outward. Separating the swollen envelope from the core left me with this bloated fog.

white_dwarf_core.flavour: What remains when a modest star sheds its outer layers: a core of carbon and oxygen about the size of the Earth, held up against gravity only by electron degeneracy pressure. It is fiercely hot and absurdly heavy for its size, and will cool for longer than the universe has existed.
white_dwarf_core.discovery: After the red giant phase, the Nucleosynthesis Chamber left a small, glowing ember behind. Electron degeneracy held it up, exactly as Chandrasekhar described, and it slowly radiated away its leftover heat.

stellar_iron_ingot.flavour: Iron forged in the core of a star, where fusion stops being profitable. Iron has the most tightly bound nucleus, so fusing it or splitting it costs energy. The ingot is dense and dull grey and carries a faint heat that seems to come from somewhere deep inside it.
stellar_iron_ingot.discovery: Combining a white dwarf core with ordinary iron in stellar plasma, I drove fusion until it stopped. Iron was where nucleosynthesis ended, and the Chamber left me an ingot of star-forged metal.

supernova_remnant.flavour: The expanding shell of gas and the collapsed core left when a massive star's core can no longer support itself. The shockwave seeds space with heavy elements. This remnant is a dense nugget wrapped in a faint, glowing haze of debris.
supernova_remnant.discovery: In the Neutron Star Forge I collapsed a stellar iron core under neutronium pressure and flooded it with neutrinos. The red giant envelope blew outward and left a small, heavy remnant.

r_process_cluster.flavour: Gold, platinum and uranium, made in seconds when a supernova or neutron star merger floods nuclei with neutrons faster than they can decay. The cluster is a dense jumble of heavy metal nuggets, gleaming in several colours at once.
r_process_cluster.discovery: Firing neutrino flux and a sterile neutrino at a supernova remnant in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber, I saw nuclei capturing neutrons faster than they could decay. Heavy elements formed in a single flash.

kaluza_klein_shard.flavour: Kaluza and Klein noticed that general relativity in five dimensions, with one dimension curled up small, produces electromagnetism for free. Momentum around that hidden circle appears as electric charge. The shard has a faint static charge and seems to hum slightly when spun.
kaluza_klein_shard.discovery: I first found these in the Bulk, among Brane Strider remains and derelict stations. Running bulk stone through Maxwell's Demon Sorter with helium, I could separate grains with momentum in the fifth dimension.

dilaton_crystal.flavour: In string theory, the dilaton is a field whose value sets the string coupling: how readily strings split and join. This crystal froze one value of it. Hold it up to the light and everything behind it looks slightly more or less substantial.
dilaton_crystal.discovery: I found these growing on the Graviton Reefs of the Bulk and inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Their facets responded to string interactions, and I realised they had frozen the dilaton field in place.

moduli_crystal.flavour: The extra dimensions of string theory have shapes and sizes set by fields called moduli. This crystal is those parameters frozen solid: a record of exactly how the hidden dimensions are curled. It changes shape slightly depending on the angle you view it from.
moduli_crystal.discovery: Moduli Crawlers in the Moduli Wastes of the Bulk dropped these, and more lay inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Measuring their facets, I found they recorded the shape and size of the compact dimensions.

brane_tension_fiber.flavour: A thread pulled from a brane, the membrane on which strings end. It is strong beyond any material, because its tension is a property of spacetime rather than chemistry. It hums faintly and pulls back toward the surface it came from.
brane_tension_fiber.discovery: Brane Striders walk on membranes in the Bulk, and when they fell they left these threads behind. I found more in derelict stations, still taut as if attached to something invisible.

graviton_wisp_core.flavour: The heart of a Graviton Wisp: a closed loop of string vibrating in the mode that makes a graviton. Even out of the Wisp, it pulls gently on everything nearby. It is light, but holding it gives a faint sensation of falling toward it.
graviton_wisp_core.discovery: Graviton Wisps drift through the Bulk, and when one dissipated it left this behind. I found more in the Calabi-Yau Knot, still faintly attracting dust.

compactified_circle.flavour: A whole dimension rolled into a circle smaller than the Planck length. Move around it and you return to where you started almost instantly. String theory needs six or seven of these to hide the extra dimensions. It looks like a dot, but feels like a loop.
compactified_circle.discovery: The Compactification Lathe spun a Kaluza-Klein shard and a quantum string until the fifth dimension curled into a tiny circle. Exotic matter held it there. I have also found them in the Calabi-Yau Knot.

string_coupling_crystal.flavour: Turn this crystal and the strength with which strings interact changes. Turn it far enough and a strongly coupled string theory becomes a weakly coupled one of a different type: this is string duality. It is cool and smooth and feels slightly alive.
string_coupling_crystal.discovery: I fixed a compactified circle's radius with a bulk crystal and varied the coupling in the Compactification Lathe. At strong coupling, Type IIA became M-theory, and the crystal captured the transition.

d_brane_sheet.flavour: A surface on which open strings can end, with its own dynamics and its own charge. Our universe could be a three-dimensional D-brane floating in higher dimensions. The sheet ripples like silk, and strings seem to cling to it.
d_brane_sheet.discovery: Stretching quantum strings across metamaterial with brane tension fiber in the Compactification Lathe, I noticed their ends stuck to the sheet. Exotic matter held it rigid enough to keep.

g2_manifold.flavour: Seven curled dimensions with a special holonomy whose symmetry group, G2, is the automorphism group of the octonions. M-theory on such a space gives a four-dimensional world with realistic physics. The manifold is tightly folded and seems to have no inside or outside.
g2_manifold.discovery: Combining a Calabi-Yau with an extra moduli direction and the octonions' symmetry, the Compactification Lathe produced a seven-dimensional manifold with G2 holonomy, held open by exotic matter.

m_theory_core.flavour: Five superstring theories turned out to be limits of one eleven-dimensional theory, whose fundamental objects include membranes as well as strings. Witten called it M-theory, and nobody knows what the M stands for. The core vibrates in more directions than seem possible.
m_theory_core.discovery: Wrapping an M-brane on a G2 manifold and a compactified circle in the Compactification Lathe, I found all five string theories as limits of one. Exotic matter kept the eleventh dimension open.

arrow_of_time_shard.flavour: Entropy increases, and that is essentially all that distinguishes the future from the past. This shard is a piece of the arrow itself, pointing the wrong way: nearby, broken things almost seem to want to mend. It is slightly cold, as though it gives up heat.
arrow_of_time_shard.discovery: A negentropy cell reverses local entropy, and a chronon capacitor stores time. Combined with chronon gas in the Chrono Loom, they produced a shard whose arrow pointed backward.

temporal_knot.flavour: A worldline tied in a knot so that an event connects to itself through time. Untying it would make something happen twice. The knot feels tight and tense, and looking at it gives a faint sense of deja vu.
temporal_knot.discovery: Twisting a backward arrow-of-time shard through a Mobius strip and pinning it with a tachyon crystal in the Chrono Loom, I tied a worldline into a closed knot. Chronon gas kept the loop stable.

novikov_crystal.flavour: Novikov's self-consistency principle states that any time loop must be consistent: events in it cannot contradict each other. This crystal enforces it. Any loop it joins sorts itself into a history with no paradoxes, and it feels calm and immovable.
novikov_crystal.discovery: A temporal knot kept threatening paradoxes. Feeding it a formal proof tree and a Lorentz crystal in the Chrono Loom, I found a solution where every event agreed with itself, and it crystallised.

wave_packet.flavour: A localised bump made by adding waves of slightly different frequencies so they reinforce in one place and cancel elsewhere. Quantum particles are wave packets, which is why their position and momentum cannot both be sharp. The packet seems to spread slowly the longer you watch it.
wave_packet.discovery: Adding up a Fourier series of entangled photon modes in the Analytic Continuator, I built a pulse of light localised in space. Its spread in frequency and position balanced exactly as Heisenberg said.

spinor_lattice.flavour: Spinors describe electrons and other spin-half particles. Rotate one a full 360 degrees and it comes back with its sign flipped; a second full turn restores it. The lattice feels oddly twisted and never quite seems to have come back to where it started.
spinor_lattice.discovery: Representing rotations with quaternions in the Peano Arithmetic Engine, I noticed each rotation had two quaternions, plus and minus. A qubit stored the sign, and the result behaved like a spinor.

quantum_field_lattice.flavour: A field spread throughout spacetime, with particles appearing as quantised excitations of it. Every electron in the universe is a ripple in a single electron field. The lattice glows faintly and seems to ripple when breathed on.
quantum_field_lattice.discovery: Placing wave packets and spinors onto a differential manifold and cooling them in a condensate, I found the Analytic Continuator could describe them all as excitations of one field.

feynman_diagram.flavour: A picture standing for a term in the calculation of how particles interact: lines are particles, vertices are interactions. Sum all diagrams and you get the full answer. The diagram moves slightly, lines bending and joining as if acting out a process.
feynman_diagram.discovery: Integrating over all the ways gauge bosons could interact with a quantum field lattice and a wavefunction, the Formal Proof Assistant returned a sum of diagrams, each a possible history of the process.

mathematics_singularity.flavour: Counting, the complex plane, the octonions, the primes, fractal boundaries and the first infinities beyond counting, all folded into one point. It has no size, yet every theorem I have ever proved seems to be somewhere inside it. Staring at it too long makes ordinary arithmetic feel quaint.
mathematics_singularity.discovery: With the Conceptual Singularity Compressor running, I fed it the cornerstones of every branch of mathematics I had built, from the natural numbers to epsilon-naught. They converged on a single point that still contained them all.

standard_model_singularity.flavour: Every quark flavour, every lepton, every force carrier and the Higgs, compressed past the point where they are separate particles. It hums with all the interactions at once. Small enough to vanish in the hand, it nevertheless feels as if it holds the entire periodic table in reserve.
standard_model_singularity.discovery: I gave the Conceptual Singularity Compressor each generation of quarks, the leptons, the gauge bosons and the Higgs, and asked it to compress the zoo. The particles collapsed into a single point carrying the whole Standard Model.

spacetime_singularity.flavour: All of relativity, from Lorentz transformations to the field equations and the stress-energy that sources them, squeezed into the one place where relativity itself predicts its own breakdown. Clocks near it disagree with each other, and straight lines bend toward it.
spacetime_singularity.discovery: Relativity predicts singularities but cannot describe them. Feeding the Compressor every tensor and transformation I had derived, I let the theory collapse onto the exact point where it fails, and kept that point.

stellar_singularity.flavour: Birth, life and death of a star, from protostar to remnant, in one point of light that never dims. Holding it is like holding a star's whole history: the warmth of fusion, the swelling of a giant and the cold heaviness of collapse, all at once and all faint.
stellar_singularity.discovery: I loaded the Compressor with every stage of stellar evolution I had produced, from protostar core to supernova remnant. The stages merged into one luminous point that remembered all of them.

dimensional_singularity.flavour: Eleven dimensions, with all their compactified circles, branes and moduli, compressed into a point with none at all. It is impossible to say which way it faces. Even the space around it seems to lose a direction or two when it is near.
dimensional_singularity.discovery: I gave the Compressor everything that held the extra dimensions in place: Kaluza-Klein shards, the dilaton, moduli, a D-brane, a penteract and a Calabi-Yau. Every dimension curled up until none remained.

temporal_singularity.flavour: Every moment collapsed into a single instant, with no before or after. Clocks stop being meaningful near it, and holding it gives a strange impression of remembering things that have not happened yet. It is perfectly still, and that stillness feels like waiting.
temporal_singularity.discovery: Feeding the Compressor every time artefact I had built, from a backward arrow to a closed timelike curve, I compressed history itself. All the instants fell into one and stayed there.

quantum_singularity.flavour: Every possible state of every quantum system, in superposition and compressed to one point. It is not in any definite state, and looking at it seems to collapse it differently each time. It flickers between being there and not.
quantum_singularity.discovery: I compressed the wavefunction, superpositions, entangled pairs, wave packets, spinors and fields together. Every possible outcome fell into the same point without any of them being chosen.

cognitive_singularity.flavour: Every thought that could be thought, from a single neural lattice up to a superintelligence and a Boltzmann brain, compressed into one point. It feels attentive. Holding it, I am briefly aware of ideas I have not had yet, and then they are gone.
cognitive_singularity.discovery: I fed every model of mind I had built into the Compressor, from neural lattices to general AI cores and holographic matrices. Thought itself collapsed to a single, watchful point.

exotic_matter_singularity.flavour: Negative mass, massless alloy, antimatter, strange matter, dark matter: every substance that should not exist, compressed together. They ought to annihilate each other or fly apart. Instead they sit in uneasy balance, and the point seems to push and pull at once.
exotic_matter_singularity.discovery: I gathered every form of exotic matter and fed them into the Compressor together, half expecting an explosion. Negative mass cancelled the rest, and they settled into one strangely stable point.

theory_of_everything.flavour: The Standard Model, quantum mechanics, relativity, string theory, grand unification and M-theory written as one equation. It is short, symmetric and almost embarrassingly simple, and it describes every interaction there is. Holding it, nothing feels mysterious, briefly.
theory_of_everything.discovery: I fed the Compressor the singularities of the Standard Model, spacetime, quantum mechanics and the extra dimensions, plus the unified cores. The theories merged. What remained fit on a single line.

omniscience_catalyst.flavour: Physics, mathematics, the stars, time, mind and exotic matter, every singularity of knowledge fused into one catalyst. Holding it, for an instant you understand everything that is the case. Then the knowledge fades, leaving a sense of having forgotten something enormous.
omniscience_catalyst.discovery: On the Extreme Assembly Table, I combined the Theory of Everything with every other conceptual singularity I had compressed. They fused into a catalyst that let me glimpse everything for a moment.

omnium_ingot.flavour: A metal made of every concept, every material and every law, distilled into one bar. It has every property and none of them, depending on what you need. It is warm, cold, light and heavy at once, and feels like the end of the line.
omnium_ingot.discovery: The Omnium block was too dense to shape, so I cracked a single ingot back out of it at the crafting grid. Whatever else I make from here, it starts with this.

platonic_compass.flavour: A compass that points not north but toward the realm of ideal mathematical forms, where numbers and shapes exist as objects. Used, it takes its bearer there, and back again. The needle trembles near anything perfectly geometric.
platonic_compass.discovery: Combining an ender eye with an axiom schema and the natural and integer lattices, I built a compass that sought pure form instead of strongholds. I have also found them in Euclid's vault and Hilbert's archives.

iron_singularity.flavour: A mountain of iron, crushed until it collapsed into a single point. It is still recognisably iron: grey, cold and faintly magnetic. Holding it feels like holding the core of a planet, and it tugs at nearby metal.
iron_singularity.discovery: I fed the Singularity Compactor iron ingots until their atoms could no longer stay apart. The pressure crushed them past degeneracy into a single dense point.

gold_singularity.flavour: An immense hoard of gold, collapsed into one gleaming point. The warmth of the metal survives, and it gives off a soft yellow glow. Every ounce of it was originally forged in neutron star collisions, and now it is all in one place again.
gold_singularity.discovery: Gold came from neutron star mergers, so it seemed fitting to crush it back down. The Singularity Compactor squeezed a pile of ingots into a single bright point.

copper_singularity.flavour: A great heap of copper crushed into a single point. It has a reddish glow, and electricity seems to pass through it without resistance. It is heavy and smooth and smells faintly of pennies. Verdigris never forms on it; there is no surface left to oxidise.
copper_singularity.discovery: Copper is cheap and plentiful, so it was easy to feed the Singularity Compactor enough of it. The ingots collapsed into a single conductive point.

coal_singularity.flavour: An enormous pile of coal compressed into one point, pure carbon squeezed far past the pressure at which coal becomes diamond. It is jet black, and the stored chemical energy of ancient forests is almost palpable.
coal_singularity.discovery: Coal is carbon from ancient plants, so I crushed vast amounts of it in the Singularity Compactor. It passed through graphite and diamond and kept going until it was a single point.

redstone_singularity.flavour: Redstone dust in such quantity that it collapsed into a single point. It glows a pulsing red and seems to carry a faint signal, as though waiting to switch something on. Its warmth fluctuates rhythmically.
redstone_singularity.discovery: I wanted to know what redstone's strange conductivity would do under extreme pressure. The Singularity Compactor crushed a mountain of dust into a single pulsing point.

lapis_singularity.flavour: Lapis lazuli in such quantity that it collapsed into one point. It is a deep, perfect blue, and the colour seems to go down forever. Holding it feels cool and calm, like the bottom of the sea. Old painters ground this stone for ultramarine, the costliest blue there was.
lapis_singularity.discovery: Lapis is mostly lazurite, a complex silicate. I fed the Singularity Compactor enough of it that the crystal lattice collapsed into a single deep-blue point.

quartz_singularity.flavour: Nether quartz crushed into one point, its crystal lattice compressed until it has no edges at all. It is milky white and faintly warm. Squeezing it seems to produce a tiny piezoelectric spark. Every vibration in the room seems to pass through it and come out sharper.
quartz_singularity.discovery: Quartz becomes electric when squeezed, so I squeezed as much as I could in the Singularity Compactor. The crystals collapsed together into a single, faintly charged point.

glowstone_singularity.flavour: Glowstone dust compacted into one point, glowing so brightly it is hard to look at directly. It is warm and seems to light everything near it. Its light flickers slightly, as if keeping time. Shadows do not quite form behind it, as if the light wraps round.
glowstone_singularity.discovery: Glowstone gives off light without burning, so I wondered what happened if it was compressed. The Singularity Compactor crushed it into a point that shone far brighter than the original dust.

amethyst_singularity.flavour: Amethyst shards compressed into a single violet point. It rings softly when tapped, like a crystal bell, and the sound seems to come from all around. Purple light refracts out of it in all directions.
amethyst_singularity.discovery: Amethyst grows in geodes and chimes when struck. Feeding enough shards into the Singularity Compactor, I crushed them into a single ringing point.

diamond_singularity.flavour: A hoard of diamonds crushed into a single brilliant point. Diamond is already carbon at its hardest; compressed further, it becomes something harder still. It scatters light into every colour and is cold to the touch.
diamond_singularity.discovery: Diamonds are carbon under pressure, so I applied more pressure. The Singularity Compactor crushed the gems into a single blazing point that scratches anything.

emerald_singularity.flavour: Emeralds crushed into one bright green point. It is perfectly clear and seems to carry a faint scent of trade and villages. Light passing through it turns a deep, satisfying green. Every facet has merged into one, and yet it still seems faceted.
emerald_singularity.discovery: Emeralds are beryl coloured by chromium. I crushed a hoard of them in the Singularity Compactor until the crystal lattice collapsed into one brilliant green point.

netherite_singularity.flavour: Netherite crushed into a single point. It is dark and dense, already the heaviest metal I had, now heavier still. It does not burn and it does not scratch, and holding it feels unshakeable. Lava slides off it and it stays exactly the temperature it was.
netherite_singularity.discovery: Netherite is ancient debris and gold, already immensely tough. I fed what I had into the Singularity Compactor and it collapsed into a single, unbreakable point.

obsidian_singularity.flavour: Obsidian compacted into one point. It is black volcanic glass, already hard to break, now impossible. Its surface reflects things that are not there, and it is faintly warm, as if still cooling from the lava.
obsidian_singularity.discovery: Obsidian is lava cooled too fast to crystallise. I fed the Singularity Compactor a quarry's worth of it, and the glass collapsed into a single dark point.

blue_ice_singularity.flavour: Blue ice compacted into a single point so cold it frosts the air around it. Normal ice melts; this does not. It is perfectly clear and blue, and slides across any surface with no friction at all. Water that touches it freezes instantly into perfect hexagons.
blue_ice_singularity.discovery: Blue ice is ice compressed until the bubbles are gone. Compressing it further in the Singularity Compactor gave me a single, freezing point that refuses to melt.

neutronium_singularity.flavour: Neutronium is already matter at nuclear density. Compressed beyond even that, it is close to becoming a true black hole. The point is perfectly black and unthinkably heavy, and space seems to dip toward it.
neutronium_singularity.discovery: Neutronium is what a neutron star is made of. Compressing it further in the Singularity Compactor brought it close to the Schwarzschild radius, and it collapsed into a single point.

cherenkov_singularity.flavour: Cherenkov quartz compressed into one point, glowing the electric blue of particles outrunning light in a medium. It flickers as if something inside is still moving faster than its own light. It is the light of a nuclear reactor pool, held in one hand.
cherenkov_singularity.discovery: Cherenkov quartz glows blue where particles move faster than light can in it. Compressing it in the Singularity Compactor focused that glow into a single brilliant point.

void_lattice_singularity.flavour: Void lattice crushed into one point. It is made of crystallised emptiness, and compressing nothing turns out to yield something very strange. The point is hard to look at, because there is nothing there to focus on.
void_lattice_singularity.discovery: Void lattice is a crystal of the vacuum. Compressing it in the Singularity Compactor, I expected nothing; I got a point that seemed to absorb its surroundings.

dilithium_singularity.flavour: Dilithium crystals compacted into a single point. They regulate high-energy reactions, and the singularity carries a faint thrum, as if still waiting to channel something. It glows a pale pink. Nearby energy seems to steady itself, as though being supervised.
dilithium_singularity.discovery: Dilithium regulates matter-antimatter reactions. Crushing enough crystals in the Singularity Compactor, I made a single point that hums with stored control.

chronosteel_singularity.flavour: Chronosteel compressed into one point, its time-hardened structure collapsed together. Time behaves oddly around it, ticking slightly faster or slower depending on how you hold it. It is cool and dense and smells faintly of rust.
chronosteel_singularity.discovery: Chronosteel is steel tempered in time. I compressed enough of it in the Singularity Compactor that its timelines merged into a single point.

stellar_iron_singularity.flavour: Star-forged iron compacted into one point. It is the end of fusion, now crushed even further. It is dense and dull grey, and carries a faint warmth from the stellar core where it formed. A compass needle swings toward it from across the room.
stellar_iron_singularity.discovery: Stellar iron is where fusion stops. I crushed enough of it in the Singularity Compactor that it collapsed into a single point, the ultimate end of a star's life.

prime_singularity.flavour: Prime shards compressed into one point. Primes cannot be divided, and the singularity seems to have inherited that indivisibility. It is perfectly smooth and cannot be split or cut by anything. Every attempt to halve it simply returns the whole thing again.
prime_singularity.discovery: Primes cannot be factored, so I wondered if they could be compressed. The Singularity Compactor forced countless shards into one point that is still, somehow, prime.

kaluza_klein_singularity.flavour: Kaluza-Klein shards compacted into a single point, their fifth-dimensional momentum crushed together. The point crackles with faint static and spins slowly around an axis that does not seem to exist in three dimensions.
kaluza_klein_singularity.discovery: Each Kaluza-Klein shard carries momentum around a hidden dimension. Compressing enough of them in the Singularity Compactor, I folded that dimension into a single charged point.

tachyon_singularity.flavour: Tachyon crystals crushed into a single point that seems to arrive before it is placed. Tachyons move faster than light, and this point moves faster still. It is cold, faintly blue, and seems to be leaving.
tachyon_singularity.discovery: Tachyons can never slow below light speed. Crushing tachyon crystals in the Singularity Compactor gave me a point that seems to be everywhere it will be, slightly early.

strange_matter_singularity.flavour: Strange matter pellets crushed into a single point. Strange matter may be the true ground state of matter, converting anything it touches. This point seems eager, and I keep it well away from anything else.
strange_matter_singularity.discovery: Strange matter could convert ordinary matter on contact. Compressing enough of it in the Singularity Compactor, I made a single point that is, so far, content to stay put.

antimatter_singularity.flavour: Antimatter compressed into a single point without touching any matter, which ought to be impossible. It holds an almost unimaginable amount of energy. It glows faintly and must never be dropped. It is kept in a magnetic cradle and checked on more often than strictly necessary.
antimatter_singularity.discovery: Antimatter annihilates on contact, so compressing it took careful magnetic fields. The Singularity Compactor eventually crushed the pellets into one point without letting them touch anything.

exotic_crystal_singularity.flavour: Exotic matter crystals compressed into one point. Exotic matter has negative energy density, and the singularity seems to push space away from itself slightly. It is faintly repellent to the touch. Dropped, it falls slowly, as though the floor were pushing back.
exotic_crystal_singularity.discovery: Exotic matter holds wormholes open. Compressing it in the Singularity Compactor, I made a single point that pushes everything else away.

spacetime_alloy_singularity.flavour: Spacetime alloy crushed into a single point, its woven space and time folded inward. Distances near it seem shorter than they should, and time seems to skip. It feels slightly warped. A ruler laid beside it reads a slightly different length every time.
spacetime_alloy_singularity.discovery: Spacetime alloy is metal woven with spacetime. Compressing it in the Singularity Compactor, I folded its spacetime inward into a single point.

computronium_singularity.flavour: Computronium compacted into a single point, matter optimised for computation crushed together. It processes constantly and feels warm with the heat of erased bits. It seems to be thinking about something.
computronium_singularity.discovery: Computronium is matter arranged to compute as efficiently as possible. Compressing it in the Singularity Compactor gave a single point running more calculations than I can count.

cosmic_neutronium_singularity.flavour: Cosmic neutronium compressed into a single point. It was already one of the densest materials I had, and now it is denser. The point is absolutely black and impossibly heavy, and space visibly dips toward it.
cosmic_neutronium_singularity.discovery: Cosmic neutronium is neutron-star matter enhanced further. I crushed it in the Singularity Compactor, and it collapsed into a single point almost too heavy to move.

cherenkov_lattice.flavour: Diamond struts and threads of Cherenkov quartz, wound around a core of netherite scrap. The quartz glows the same blue that charged particles give off when they outrun light in water. It is a frame for a crystal that cannot hold itself together, rigid and faintly luminous.
cherenkov_lattice.discovery: I needed scaffolding strong enough to pin a superposition in place. Diamond for rigidity, netherite for weight and Cherenkov quartz to keep the light moving gave me a frame that would not flinch.

crystalline_matrix_ingot.flavour: A superposition crystal locked inside a Cherenkov lattice and fixed there by the light of a nether star. The ingot is glassy but metal-heavy, and its interior shows several overlapping lattices at once, none of them willing to collapse into the others.
crystalline_matrix_ingot.discovery: Superposition crystals collapse when observed, so I sealed one inside a Cherenkov lattice and bathed it in the light of a dead star on the Extreme Assembly Table. The lattices froze mid-superposition.

biosphere_compendium.flavour: Beef, pork, chicken, mutton, rabbit and cod, every edible animal pressed into one dense block. It smells of a farmyard, a kitchen and a fishing dock all at once. It is technically food, and absolutely not for eating.
biosphere_compendium.discovery: Building the catalyst meant compressing every field of knowledge, including biology. On the Extreme Assembly Table I pressed one of each edible creature together into a single record of the food chain.

primordial_harvest.flavour: Wheat, carrot, potato, beetroot, melon and pumpkin, every staple crop combined into a single seed. It is warm and slightly damp and seems ready to sprout into all of them at once. Planting it would probably be unwise.
primordial_harvest.discovery: Agriculture belonged in the catalyst too, so I pressed every crop I could grow into one seed on the Extreme Assembly Table. It holds the genome of a whole harvest.

hyperdimensional_pearl.flavour: An ender pearl wrapped in bulk stone and cosmic neutronium and charged by a nether star. Thrown, an ordinary pearl takes you somewhere; this one would take you everywhere. It shimmers and is never quite in the place it appears to be.
hyperdimensional_pearl.discovery: Ender pearls teleport through some hidden dimension. Wrapping one in bulk stone gave it access to all of them, and a nether star kept it from scattering on the Extreme Assembly Table.

cosmic_record_fragment.flavour: A sliver of a disc that recorded the Big Bang, cut from Cherenkov quartz and neutronium. Play it and you hear the cosmic microwave background, a faint hiss left from the first moments of everything. It is cool and heavy, and vibrates faintly.
cosmic_record_fragment.discovery: Cherenkov quartz responds to fast particles; neutronium records pressure. Pressing them together on the Extreme Assembly Table, I found the fragment picked up the oldest signal in the universe.

virtual_quark.flavour: A quark borrowed from the vacuum, existing only on credit granted by the uncertainty principle. The more energy it has, the sooner it must be returned. It tugs constantly at the hand, trying to fall back into nothing.
virtual_quark.discovery: Virtual Pairs in the Quantum Foam dropped these when they split. Later, the Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester let me pull them from between Casimir plates and keep them cold enough to stay.

virtual_graviton.flavour: A quantum of gravity that has not decided to exist yet, flickering between being and not being. It pulls faintly on everything near it, and then on nothing. Nobody has ever detected a real graviton; this one is not quite real.
virtual_graviton.discovery: Vacuum Drifters in the Quantum Foam dropped these when killed. The Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester let me catch more from between Casimir plates, cooled with superfluid helium.

virtual_photon.flavour: Light that was never emitted and will never be absorbed, existing only between two charges as the carrier of their force. It glows faintly from no direction in particular and vanishes from view when looked at directly.
virtual_photon.discovery: Virtual Pairs left these behind in the Quantum Foam. Later I harvested them from between Casimir plates, where they press the plates together in the Casimir effect.

virtual_monopole.flavour: A magnet with only one pole, borrowed from the vacuum and destined to return. Real monopoles have never been found, though grand unified theories predict them. This one pushes one end of a compass needle away and never pulls the other.
virtual_monopole.discovery: Planck Mites in the Quantum Foam dropped these. Harvesting more from between Casimir plates, I found they only lasted as long as the superfluid helium kept them cold.

planck_diver.flavour: A device that shrinks its bearer below the Planck length, into the Quantum Foam where spacetime itself is a boiling froth. Used again, it brings you back. It feels light and fragile, but it has survived the trip every time so far.
planck_diver.discovery: I needed to go where the vacuum fluctuates, so I combined a brane shifter, a Planck shard and graviton crystal around a chronosteel frame on the Extreme Assembly Table. It shrank me past the Planck scale.

resonance_probe.flavour: A handheld instrument that reads the four virtual-particle resonances of the Quantum Foam where you stand. It hums at different pitches depending on what the vacuum is doing, and its needle never settles.
resonance_probe.discovery: In the Quantum Foam I needed to know which virtual particles were bubbling up where. A spectral analyzer tuned by a qubit and a Planck shard gave me a probe that could read the foam's resonances.

omnium_singularity.flavour: A hoard of Omnium Ingots crushed into a single point, every concept compressed into one place. There is nothing left beyond it to compress it into. It is everything and nothing, and holding it feels final.
omnium_singularity.discovery: I fed the Singularity Compactor Omnium Ingots until even they collapsed. The result was a point containing everything there is. I am not sure there is anything left to build.

fractal_core.flavour: The innermost copy of a Fractal Wyrm, which by self-similarity is also the outermost. It is a perfect miniature of the Wyrm, coiled within itself, and its edges recede infinitely as you look at them. It is never still for long.
fractal_core.discovery: I took this from a fallen Fractal Wyrm, and found another in the Hilbert Archive. Zooming in, it contained a smaller Wyrm, which contained a smaller one, and so on forever.

proof_fragment.flavour: A piece of a formal proof an Axiom Sentinel was writing, apparently about me. The lines are rigorous and the conclusion is clear, though the middle steps are missing. It feels like being judged. I have not yet found the missing lemmas.
proof_fragment.discovery: Axiom Sentinels drop these when defeated, and I found more in the Hilbert Archive. Reading one closely, I found it was proving something about my own existence.

wavefunction.flavour: Everything a particle could be, written as one complex-valued function. Its square gives the probability of finding the particle anywhere. The function hovers above the palm as a faint, shifting haze that never settles into one shape.
wavefunction.discovery: Combining a qubit with the complex plane on a foam substrate, and adding Schrodinger's Limit, I described a particle's state completely. The Analytic Continuator called it a wavefunction.

hamiltonian_operator.flavour: The operator that answers how a quantum system evolves by telling you its energy. Schrodinger's equation is just the statement that the Hamiltonian drives time evolution. It is calm and steady, ticking quietly.
hamiltonian_operator.discovery: Differentiating a wavefunction with respect to time, I found the rate of change was proportional to energy. The Analytic Continuator packaged that rule into an operator.

eigenstate_lattice.flavour: The particular states in which a measurement gives a definite value. Measure the energy, and the system will be found in one of these, no matter what it was before. The lattice is regular and seems quieter than its surroundings.
eigenstate_lattice.discovery: Applying the Hamiltonian to spinors and virtual photons, I searched for states it left unchanged except for a number. The Analytic Continuator arranged them into a lattice.

path_integral.flavour: Feynman's insight: a particle takes every possible path at once, and the probabilities add up with phases. Most paths cancel; the classical one survives. The integral shimmers with countless faint trails, all overlapping.
path_integral.discovery: Summing virtual quark trajectories weighted by the Hamiltonian, I found that the straight paths dominated while the rest cancelled. The Analytic Continuator kept them all.

geodesic_thread.flavour: The straightest line possible in curved spacetime: the path a falling object takes. Around a black hole, geodesics curve, spiral and close in. The thread bends according to the gravity around it and never kinks.
geodesic_thread.discovery: Inside a black hole, a geodesic is the only safe path. Following one with neutronium and the real continuum in the Chrono Loom, I wove relativity breakdown into a thread that always falls straight.

christoffel_symbol.flavour: A record of how coordinates twist from point to point on a curved space. It is not a tensor, but it tells you how vectors change as you carry them along. The symbol looks slightly different each time you turn it.
christoffel_symbol.discovery: Differentiating geodesic threads with a Koch crystal's self-similarity, I tracked how coordinates bent near the horizon. The Chrono Loom produced the connection coefficients.

stress_energy_tensor.flavour: The tensor describing how energy, momentum and pressure are distributed in spacetime: the source term of Einstein's equations. It is heavy in some directions and light in others, and seems to press against the hand.
stress_energy_tensor.discovery: Combining Christoffel symbols with a stellar core and a frozen photon, I described how mass-energy filled spacetime. The Chrono Loom gave me the tensor that tells spacetime how to curve.

einstein_rosen_core.flavour: Both mouths of a bridge between a black hole and a white hole, held together in one object. Einstein and Rosen found that black hole solutions connect two regions of spacetime. The core pulls in at one end and pushes out at the other.
einstein_rosen_core.discovery: Inside a black hole, I found tidal scrap; inside a white hole, primordial ejecta. Joining them in the Tesseract Assembler with retrocausal crystal and a frozen photon, I built the bridge.

tidal_alloy_scrap.flavour: Metal stretched thin by tidal forces stronger than its chemical bonds: spaghettification in action. It is long, thin and flexible, and still faintly stretched in one direction. It feels like it is being pulled.
tidal_alloy_scrap.discovery: Tidal Horrors inside black holes dropped this scrap when they fell. I recognised it as metal that had been stretched apart by gravity's gradient.

frozen_photon.flavour: Light that reached the event horizon and stopped there, from an outside view, redshifted almost to nothing. It is barely visible and very cold, the faintest red glow, and it never quite fades away. Warming it does nothing.
frozen_photon.discovery: Tidal Horrors dropped these near the horizon. Later, I made them in the Neutron Star Forge by firing stellar plasma through infall rock against a neutronium plate.

retrocausal_crystal.flavour: A crystal that formed after it was mined, its cause later than its effect. It is perfectly ordinary in appearance, which makes its history more unnerving. Holding it, I sometimes remember mining it before I have done so.
retrocausal_crystal.discovery: Photon Moths near white holes dropped these. I mined one before I knew what it was, and only afterward did it form, exactly where my pick had been.

primordial_ejecta.flavour: Matter a white hole threw out before there was anything to throw. A white hole is a time-reversed black hole, expelling rather than swallowing. This debris is warm and ancient, and seems to be still moving outward.
primordial_ejecta.discovery: Photon Moths near white holes dropped these fragments. They were older than anything I had ever found, pushed out of a white hole before the universe began.

geodesic_anchor.flavour: A device that keeps its bearer's worldline intact inside a black or white hole. Without it, tidal forces and causal chaos are lethal within seconds. It is heavy and cool and hums faintly, like a gyroscope.
geodesic_anchor.discovery: Inside a black hole I nearly lost my worldline. Combining a Kerr metric shard, graviton crystal and chronon capacitor in a hyperlattice frame on the Extreme Assembly Table, I built an anchor to keep it.

horizon_diver.flavour: A device that carries its bearer across an event horizon, inward, and, which should be impossible, back out again. It is cool, black and heavy. Holding it gives the faint impression of falling. Its casing is always cold.
horizon_diver.discovery: To see past the horizon, I built a diver around a micro singularity and a Hawking absorber plate on the Extreme Assembly Table, with a brane shifter to find the way out again.

ordinal_shard.flavour: A piece of the order in which infinities come: first, second, third and onward past omega. Ordinals count positions, not sizes. The shard has sharp, clearly ordered facets, each following the last. No two are ever equal.
ordinal_shard.discovery: Hilbert Bellhops and Ordinal Hounds dropped these, and I found more in Hilbert's Hotel and the Ordinal Spire. Later I cut them from ordinal stone with the Planck-Scale Cutter.

cardinal_shard.flavour: A piece of how many there are, even when there are infinitely many. Cardinals measure the size of a set rather than its order. The shard is uniform and solid and feels like a count without a sequence.
cardinal_shard.discovery: Ordinal Hounds dropped these, and I found more in Hilbert's Hotel and the Ordinal Spire. They measured how big a set was, regardless of how it was ordered.

hypersphere_fragment.flavour: A curved piece of a four-dimensional sphere, whose surface is three-dimensional. In three dimensions, we see only a cross section: a ball that grows and shrinks as the fragment moves. It is smooth and seems to have more inside than out.
hypersphere_fragment.discovery: Hypercube Drifters dropped these, and I found more in Hilbert's Hotel. I realised they were pieces of a sphere with one more dimension than I could see.

omega_ordinal.flavour: The first ordinal after all the natural numbers, the first step into infinity. It comes after every finite number but is not the largest of anything. The token is smooth and plain, with no predecessor.
omega_ordinal.discovery: I counted the natural numbers in the Ordinal Recursor with ordinal shards and stone. When they ran out, the next step was omega. I also found tokens of it in the Ordinal Spire.

epsilon_naught.flavour: Omega to the omega to the omega, forever: the first ordinal that equals omega raised to itself. It is still countable, which feels absurd. The token has an endlessly recursive pattern, each layer like the last.
epsilon_naught.discovery: Raising omega to itself in the Ordinal Recursor, with power sets and ordinal shards, I reached a fixed point. Dark energy kept it from collapsing. I also found these in the Ordinal Spire.

omega_one.flavour: The first ordinal that cannot be counted, the first uncountable infinity in the order of ordinals. Every countable ordinal comes before it. The token is heavy and solid, and seems to have no edges. It refuses to be listed.
omega_one.discovery: Climbing past epsilon-naught in the Ordinal Recursor, I eventually ran out of countable ordinals. Combining aleph-null and cardinal shards with dark energy, I reached the first uncountable one.

aleph_one.flavour: The next size of infinity after the countable one: the cardinality of omega-one. Whether it equals the size of the real line is independent of the standard axioms. The token is dense and unbearably large for something that fits in a hand.
aleph_one.discovery: Measuring omega-one with cardinal shards in the Ordinal Recursor, I found the next infinity after the countable one. Synaptic fluid helped me hold the concept in mind long enough.

inaccessible_cardinal.flavour: An infinity so large no smaller infinity can build it, by unions or power sets. Its existence cannot be proved from the usual axioms. The token is heavy and remote, as if seen from a great distance. Nothing reaches it.
inaccessible_cardinal.discovery: Using a topos, aleph-one and Hilbert's Hotel key in the Cantor Diagonalizer, I tried to build a larger infinity from smaller ones. It refused, and the result was an inaccessible cardinal.

hopf_fibration.flavour: A three-sphere unwound into circles, each circle linked with every other exactly once. Hopf found it in 1931, and it appears in physics from magnetic monopoles to quantum states. It is beautiful and endlessly twisting.
hopf_fibration.discovery: Combining a hypersphere fragment with quaternions and compactified circles in the Tesseract Assembler, I found the three-sphere fibred into linked circles. I also found these in the Ordinal Spire.

penteract_lattice.flavour: A five-dimensional cube: its shadow in three dimensions is a nest of cubes connected corner to corner. Every face is a tesseract. Turning it in the hand, the faces fold through one another endlessly. It never stops turning.
penteract_lattice.discovery: Extending a tesseract core into a fifth dimension with a hypersphere fragment and Hopf fibration, the Tesseract Assembler built a penteract. Exotic matter held the extra dimension open.
